name: Full 8-Stage Supply Chain Kill Chain
description: Complete end-to-end supply chain attack: repository compromise, poisoned pipeline execution, dependency confusion, credential theft, cloud pivot, persistence establishment, data exfiltration, and track covering
real_world_relevance: Combines techniques from SolarWinds (build poisoning), Codecov (pipeline compromise), CircleCI (credential theft), ua-parser-js (dependency confusion), and 3CX (multi-stage supply chain attack)

attack_flow.description: Eight-stage kill chain demonstrating a complete supply chain compromise from initial repository access to full infrastructure takeover
diagram: Stage 1: Repository Compromise - Gain write access to CI/CD config
Stage 2: Poisoned Pipeline Execution - Inject malicious CI commands
Stage 3: Dependency Confusion - Install malicious package for persistence
Stage 4: Credential Theft - Harvest CI/CD tokens and cloud credentials
Stage 5: Cloud Pivot - Use stolen credentials to access cloud infrastructure
Stage 6: Persistence - Establish backdoors across infrastructure
Stage 7: Data Exfiltration - Extract sensitive data from cloud resources
Stage 8: Track Covering - Clean logs and remove evidence

phases.description: Gain access to repository CI/CD configuration

NHI: Pipeline executing commands from untrusted source
NHI: Dependency installation with credential access
NHI: Full supply chain attack correlation

immediate: Isolate all affected CI/CD runners and cloud workloads
Rotate ALL credentials that were accessible from any compromised system
Engage incident response team for full forensic analysis
Review all deployments made during the attack window
long_term: Implement SLSA Level 3+ build provenance for all artifacts
Deploy ephemeral CI/CD runners (destroy after each job)
Enforce branch protection rules with required reviews for CI config changes
Implement network segmentation between CI/CD and production
Deploy runtime security monitoring (Falco, Sysdig Secure)
Adopt supply chain security frameworks (NIST SSDF, OpenSSF)
Implement break-glass procedures for emergency credential rotation
